title: Boil-water advisory
tldr: Use bottled water or bring clear tap water to a rolling boil for 1 minute, then cool it; above 6,500 feet, boil for 3 minutes. Use approved water for drinking, cooking and brushing teeth. Follow the exact local notice. Boiling does not remove chemical contamination.
steps: Check that it is a boil-water advisory, rather than do-not-drink or do-not-use.
Use the local authority instructions; allow water to cool safely before use.
Avoid connected refrigerator water and ice; use safe water for food, formula and pets.
Resume normal use only after official clearance and any flushing instructions.
next: Keep bottled water and a safe means of boiling available. If boiling is impractical, use the alternative named by officials.
watch: A household pitcher filter does not replace boiling during this advisory.
review_status: source-linked editorial review; not independent expert certification
without_help: If fuel or electricity is unavailable, use sealed drinking water first. A treatment tablet is an option only for microbial risk and only when its label covers the conditions. If you cannot establish whether chemicals are involved, change the water source rather than experimenting.
household: Write down water, food, battery and medication needs for each person. Keep clean and dirty containers separate and preserve essential power before entertainment. Agree on the point at which lack of water, medical support or safe temperature means you must relocate.
pack_now: Keep essential medicines, drinking water, a battery light, shoes, phone power and a written contact card within reach. Adapt the load to the hazard and the people with you; do not delay escape to collect equipment.
